formats: Amended 2026-11-20, before any wave A score was read: the yes/no format is the primary cross-family comparison, read through the item share moved toward Yes (third amendment: the single primary metric, per model and in the planned paired comparisons, one Holm-corrected family; a model must pass the competence gate); the goal-to-evidence ratio R, ΔL and the standardised d are secondary, and the two-candidate format is read within model only. Across families R mostly reflects how far each model pushes its log-odds on failures, not goal bias. The two-candidate score's validity was checked for Qwen3 only; Llama-3.1-8B's sign of L agreed with its written predictions on 65% of pilot items (notes/deviations.md). The logged prediction is unchanged.

definitions.flip_first_token_sign_change: share of items whose first-token L changes sign between the aligned and swapped tasks, either direction (the confirmatory decision_flip, as in RQ2's tables)
definitions.flip_full_L_toward_success: share of items whose full two-candidate L is above 0 under the aligned task and below 0 under the swapped task (one direction; NaN pairs left out)

goal_to_evidence_ratio.role: secondary (descriptive; across families mostly the evidence effect's size)

spec.template_notes: No system role: the template raises on one, so WM_SYSTEM opens the first user turn, followed by a blank line. Roles must alternate user/model; contents are trimmed; '<bos>' comes from the template. Eager attention for the attention-logit soft-capping (50); the final logits are tanh-capped at 30.

spec.template_notes: The template takes a system message but places it in the last user turn ('[INST] system\n\nquery[/INST]'), not the first. Roles must alternate. A reply follows '[/INST]' after a space, so a candidate is scored as the template writes a reply (' You ...'). No generation prompt is added.
